newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals end sharply down, led by gold.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals end sharply down, led by gold.

text.p: New York precious metals ended sharply lower Monday, with gold tumbling to fresh 12-year lows. Although more than half the initial losses were pared by close, a further fall is expected, dealers said.
Most-actively traded COMEX gold settled down $6.20 at $319.00 an ounce, traded $320.60 to $314.60. Volume was estimated at 42,000 lots.
Monday's losses followed a $7.10 drop last Thursday when Reserve Bank of Australia said it had sold most of its gold reserves, suggesting there were better returns elsewhere.
COMEX was closed Friday in observance of U.S. Independence Day.
The two-session plunge in gold was due to speculators selling the market short, gambling that prices would go lower, dealers said.

According to the CFTC Commitment of Traders report to week ended July 1, two days before Thursday's initial selloff, non-commercials or speculators were already massively short, holding 72,241 short positions and just 5,230 long positions.
The commercials were heavily long, with 139,801 long positions and 69,136 short positions.
Analyst Jim Steel of Refco said Monday's losses were pared by shortcovering rather than fresh buying.
"It's just bargain-hunting," Steel said.
Scott Mehlman, chief dealer at Credit Lyonnais Rouse, said the market was expected to retest $314.10 an ounce in spot metal.
"Underneath $300 is entirely possible," Mehlman said. "There may be some shortcovering rallies but they will be worth selling."
Trading at NYMEX's new state of the art facility in Battery Park City, Manhattan began Monday after the move during Independence Day weekend from the World Trade Center.
Floor sources said glitches with the new telephone system, which NYMEX said would be resolved by Tuesday, caused some frustration during the early selloff in gold.
The selloff was the continuation of a well-established downward trend in gold prices as a growing list of central banks sell the yellow metal, dealers said.
The Philadelphia Stock Exchange's Gold and Silver mining stocks index slumped about 9 percent Monday, down 7.88 points at 86.82 late afternoon as gold producer equities took a hammering.

COMEX September silver tumbled more than 30 cents to $4.25 an ounce, the lowest in just over four years, before recovering to end at $4.285 an ounce, down 28.5 cents on the day. Volume was estimated at 23,000 lots.
Dealers said there was no fresh fundamental news behind silver's sharp tumble which was largely on the back of gold's woes and technically-based.

Gold's downward spiral also pulled the white metals lower amid further reports quoting Russian officials saying the country's shipments of its much delayed 1997 exports of platinum and palladium would begin this month.
NYMEX October platinum went out $12.00 lower at $392.70 an ounce, traded $398.00 to $390.10.
NYMEX September palladium settled $3.25 an ounce weaker at $169.75.
((Huw Jones, New York Commodity Desk 212-859-1646))
